decisions.summary: The audit reads dev/claims-index.json and snapshots it as findings.json in the feature directory
decisions.why: Implements FR-001's 'every finding in make claims-report' and makes SC-001 checkable against the report the audit read.

decisions.summary: ranking.json (key, verdict, tier, fix, files, after, flag, wave) plus a generated ranking.md grouped by tier then module
decisions.why: FR-001 asks for a readable table and countable data; the fields are the spec's Ranking row entity.

decisions.summary: tests/test_328_ranking.py holds one row per findings.json key with a tier and a fix, and ranking.md current with the JSON
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-001/SC-001, which the spec itself asks for ('a test (or a script check)').

decisions.summary: Hamlet changes proven first on inashiro.gen.py, then the pool; Mode A sheets are hand SVGs
decisions.why: Order of verification inside FR-005's 'maps a wave changes are regenerated'; drops nothing.

decisions.summary: Nine read-only Opus batches of 47-76 findings grouped by module, from ranking-brief.md
decisions.why: How the FR-001 audit is staffed; covers every finding; the brief carries FR-002/FR-003/FR-004 and the GM's direction.

decisions.summary: E0 rows tiered on the brief's earlier unbounded wording (E0 not MISLABELED or UNCLAIMED) get a bounded re-check; they stay E0 only with a named page already saying what the code does
decisions.why: Applies FR-003's bounded E0 to rows produced before the bound; tightens toward the request, narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A row a dependency outranks takes that dependency's tier
decisions.why: Implements FR-003 'a row follows any row it depends on' and SC-003's allowance that a row may wait on a dependency; the row is still fixed, only placed after what it needs, which is the real work order for 'easiest to hardest'.

decisions.summary: A second Opus reader re-tiers 30 sampled rows blind; more than 5 rows off by more than one tier re-runs the disagreeing batch
decisions.why: The spec's Assumption that tiers are checked by a second reader on a sample; the numbers are the plan's parameters for it and remove no finding.

decisions.summary: Waves E0, E1, E2, E3, E4; within a tier by module so one bundle re-checks a module's rows; 'after' rows wait
decisions.why: FR-003 ordering and SC-003 as specified.

decisions.summary: Wave 1 is every E0 row: claim lines corrected, no map change, re-checked by impl-drift by module, gate run, no regeneration owed
decisions.why: The lowest tier first is what the request and SC-003 require; no map regeneration is owed because nothing drawn moves (FR-005 owes it only for changed maps).

decisions.summary: Only the current wave's rows are task boxes; the next wave is appended as an amendment reviewed on a reset counter
E1 by module (reference hamlet then pool), E2, E3 including Mode A sheets, E4 with a research pass first
decisions.why: FR-003 tiers, FR-009 sheets and the spec's E4 edge case, in order; nothing excluded.

decisions.summary: Rows flagged deviation-tempting go to spec-fidelity with the request verbatim before any other fix
decisions.why: FR-004 and the XVI edge case; the flag is the mechanism that routes them, and the brief tiers them by implementation work, so none is skipped.

decisions.summary: No perf bookend for wave 1; each later wave changing engine behavior takes its own start/end bookend
decisions.why: Constitution VI applied per wave; wave 1 changes no engine behavior; drops no requested work.

decisions.summary: Wave 1 behavior-free; later waves take a detached-worktree baseline per wave amendment
decisions.why: The project's regression rule applied per wave; not a narrowing of the request.
